## Purpose

Find completed task sources whose required checks are red, without moving or
reopening those tasks. Pending or unavailable evidence appears separately in
`unresolved`, so an incomplete observation cannot imply that everything passed.

## When a playbook uses it

Use it in a supervisor audit of a project's completed work or before reconciling
legacy completions. It inspects source CI; delivery and integration candidate
validation have their own controls.

## How it works internally

[`src/commands/ci_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/ci_commands.py) lists the
project's COMPLETED tasks and reads their latest completion commit. Legacy
`work_commit_auto` or `work_commit` metadata is a fallback. The observer in
[`src/integration/completion_ci.py`](../../../src/integration/completion_ci.py)
queries check runs for that exact SHA in the task's bound repository, using
project required checks or the configured merge-check fallback. Duplicate
repository/SHA/policy observations share a result within the audit.

## Side effects and persistence

This is a read-only command. It does not change task status, completion records,
claims, or delivery state. Ordinary workers cannot call it; project supervisors
remain restricted to their own project.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

An unknown project rejects the command. Missing commits, invalid policies and
unreadable GitHub evidence produce unresolved rows with an error. Missing or
running checks remain unresolved; failed checks appear in `failing` with their
names and links. A missing recorded SHA is never replaced by a moving branch
head. Projects without configured completion CI requirements are skipped.

## Example step

Invoke `ci_completed_status` with a literal project ID, save its result, and
inspect `failing` and `unresolved` on the `listed` transition. Route `rejected`
and `runtime_error` to the playbook's diagnostic path. The same read from the CLI:

```bash
aq ci completed-status --project-id agent-queue --json
```
